title: All "except" blocks should be able to catch exceptions
description: An except block that cannot catch any exceptions is misleading and serves no purpose. This can happen if the except block specifies an exception type that cannot be raised by the try block, or if the block is unreachable. Such code is confusing and should be removed or corrected.
message: This except block cannot catch any exceptions.
impact: Misleading except blocks make code harder to understand and maintain, and may hide real errors.
recommendation: Ensure that all except blocks are able to catch exceptions that can actually be raised by the corresponding try block.

noncompliant.description: The except block for ValueError will never be executed because 1/0 raises ZeroDivisionError, not ValueError.

compliant.description: The except block for ValueError can actually catch the exception raised by int('a').

why_is_this_an_issue: Except blocks that cannot catch any exceptions are misleading and serve no purpose. They make code harder to understand and may hide real errors.
how_to_fix: Review the exceptions that can be raised in the try block and ensure that the except blocks are able to catch them.

security_mappings.CWE: CWE-703: Improper Check or Handling of Exceptional Conditions
